body:
As we get close to the halfway mark of 2023, we thought it was a good moment to step back and look at the big picture. | | | Peter, As we get close to the halfway mark of 2023, we thought it was a good moment to step back and look at the big picture:
* **We’ve accomplished so much together already in the first half of 2023.** Thanks to the support of tens of thousands of WFP members, we have won some big victories in places including Chicago, Wisconsin, Pennsylvania, Colorado, Texas, Georgia, Virginia, and just yesterday in New York. The results of these elections for offices like mayors, city councils, state legislatures, and other local offices are already making a big difference in people’s lives.

* **We’ve got**** _a lot_****left to do if we’re going to get ready for the second half of 2023 and 2024.** Over the next six months, we need to power our candidates across the finish line in general elections in states like Pennsylvania and Virginia, and in primaries and special elections in other states. We also need to scale up our efforts to recruit new candidates, train campaign staff, build out our infrastructure, and be prepared to win more governing power at every level in 2024.

* **We can do all of this — but it takes resources.** We know what’s coming our way: an even bigger deluge of corporate money and right-wing attacks than we’ve ever seen before. The only way working people have ever been able to fight back against these kinds of attacks is through the support of grassroots donors like you. And early support means the most of all.

clean_body: As we get close to the halfway mark of 2023, we thought it was a good moment to step back and look at the big picture. | | | Peter, As we get close to the halfway mark of 2023, we thought it was a good moment to step back and look at the big picture: We’ve accomplished so much together already in the first half of 2023. Thanks to the support of tens of thousands of WFP members, we have won some big victories in places including Chicago, Wisconsin, Pennsylvania, Colorado, Texas, Georgia, Virginia, and just yesterday in New York. The results of these elections for offices like mayors, city councils, state legislatures, and other local offices are already making a big difference in people’s lives. We’ve got a lotleft to do if we’re going to get ready for the second half of 2023 and 2024. Over the next six months, we need to power our candidates across the finish line in general elections in states like Pennsylvania and Virginia, and in primaries and special elections in other states. We also need to scale up our efforts to recruit new candidates, train campaign staff, build out our infrastructure, and be prepared to win more governing power at every level in 2024. We can do all of this — but it takes resources. We know what’s coming our way: an even bigger deluge of corporate money and right-wing attacks than we’ve ever seen before. The only way working people have ever been able to fight back against these kinds of attacks is through the support of grassroots donors like you. And early support means the most of all. I first ran for office to make sure our government was serving hardworking Americans like my grandparents a hundred years ago.

| Hi Peter.

Here’s a photo of my grandparents, Arnfred and Christine, on their wedding day in 1905. That was seven years before they picked out a flat piece of grassland just outside Big Sandy to build their homestead.
---
[](https://click.everyaction.com/k/65580695/413913423/665036970?refcode=BLU-FFP-20230628-1-EM&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAwNS8xLzc3NDA2IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjU3MTc0NzcwLTBjMTYtZWUxMS1hOWJiLTAwMjI0ODMyZWI3MyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=DNBKf3it8jPjDkXkYF9ZMs6XgHVv4eJMDF_9K3mzQaU=)
That patch of loamy, alkaline clay-soil is the same one where I grew up; and where Sharla and I raised our kids and still farm the land.

Things weren’t easy for Fred and Christine. They suffered devastating windstorms, bitter cold, shooting fire, poisonous snakes—pretty much everything but locusts. And in the late teens, the drought hit, wiping out the farm entirely. My grandparents were forced to leave.

But they were determined to return to their homestead. They saved up enough to start all over again on the same little piece of land. They had a couple hundred acres to their name, a newly-built barn, a windmill, their healthy son and daughters (including newborn Helen, my mom), strong muscles, and the powerful work ethic that built rural America.

**I first ran for office to make sure our government was serving hardworking Americans like my grandparents a hundred years ago. Folks like our teachers, farmers, and construction workers deserve a government that works for them.**

But too many Washington politicians are deep in the pockets of right-wing special interests. They promise one thing when the camera is rolling, then make secret backroom deals with their wealthy megadonors.

That’s not how I operate, and it’s why we’re running this campaign differently. **I’m counting on grassroots folks like you chipping in what you can, when you can, to build a team strong enough to take on the outside groups and Republican attacks.**

clean_body: I first ran for office to make sure our government was serving hardworking Americans like my grandparents a hundred years ago. | Hi Peter. Here’s a photo of my grandparents, Arnfred and Christine, on their wedding day in 1905. That was seven years before they picked out a flat piece of grassland just outside Big Sandy to build their homestead. = That patch of loamy, alkaline clay-soil is the same one where I grew up; and where Sharla and I raised our kids and still farm the land. Things weren’t easy for Fred and Christine. They suffered devastating windstorms, bitter cold, shooting fire, poisonous snakes—pretty much everything but locusts. And in the late teens, the drought hit, wiping out the farm entirely. My grandparents were forced to leave. But they were determined to return to their homestead. They saved up enough to start all over again on the same little piece of land. They had a couple hundred acres to their name, a newly-built barn, a windmill, their healthy son and daughters (including newborn Helen, my mom), strong muscles, and the powerful work ethic that built rural America. I first ran for office to make sure our government was serving hardworking Americans like my grandparents a hundred years ago. Folks like our teachers, farmers, and construction workers deserve a government that works for them. But too many Washington politicians are deep in the pockets of right-wing special interests. They promise one thing when the camera is rolling, then make secret backroom deals with their wealthy megadonors. That’s not how I operate, and it’s why we’re running this campaign differently. I’m counting on grassroots folks like you chipping in what you can, when you can, to build a team strong enough to take on the outside groups and Republican attacks. = | If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately. | | = | = | = | = | = Thanks for your support. body:
Politics can be soooo icky.
#
Derek,
When I think about June, it's a busy month with the kids starting their summer break from school. But João's Finance Team told me it's also when we set an ambitious fundraising goal that impacts John's work for the rest of the year.
Politics can be soooooo icky. We saw that in the past few months, as the worst of the worst made horrible comments about João online and on Fox News. **And every time the right wing attacks, dirty corporate PAC money still flows to their side — that's one of the worst parts.**
That's why we rely 100% on clean and honest support from this people-powered team instead. It's about decency. We're proud of this team, and proud of the way we're able to help support the important things getting done in the Senate for the working people of PA.
**[So I'm asking: Will you consider making a contribution right now to help our campaign reach our goal before the big deadline in just two days? Even a few dollars would help before Friday at midnight.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-email-20230628-1?refcode=em20230628-1-8432&refcode2=8432_434096_sdTzUO&akid=8432%2E434096%2EsdTzUO)**

If enough folks chip in through emails, ads, and texts, we can hit our fundraising goal while knowing we stayed true to our movement and true to our values -- no matter what the other side might say.
**[So if you're able to chip in to help us reach our June goal, thank you sooo much!](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-email-20230628-1?refcode=em20230628-1-8432&refcode2=8432_434096_sdTzUO&akid=8432%2E434096%2EsdTzUO)** And if you can't donate, remember reading this email makes you part of our team. We really appreciate you.
With love,
Gisele ❤️
